newsitem.title: UK: Mining exploration boom seen in emerging markets.
newsitem.headline: Mining exploration boom seen in emerging markets.

text.p: A boom in mining exploration over the past few years promises to result in significant discoveries in the near future, analyst James Crombie told the Global Emerging Markets '96 conference on Thursday.
"The next seven to 10 years will be a unique moment in history with the cards unusually stacked in favour of exploration success," said Crombie, senior mining analyst for Yorkton Securities.
Expenditure on mining exploration over the past five years has increased from $1.7 billion in 1991 to $3.5 billion last year, he said.
The greatest growth in spending has been in emerging markets, which were recently considered too risky for investment.

Exploration spending in Latin American countries soared from about $140 million to $800 million in the same five year period. Africa attracted $300 million, while $250 million was spent on exploartion in the Pacific area last year, he said.
Investment funds are increasingly enthusiastic about making capital available for mining exploration, he said.
"The exploration boom is not going away," Crombie said.

New exploration finds were likely to crop up first in South America, including Peru, Ecuador, Colombia and the Guyana shield, he said. Usually exploration of mineral finds lagged behind funding by about three or four years.

In another year or two Ghana and other African countries were likely to be the site of exploration successes. Indonesia, a new favourite target for exploration, was likely to start producing results in two years.
